title: Songbook and Vow
premise: Isandro Hartwell, a wedding planner who swore off believing in love after his own engagement collapsed, agrees to a fake date with festival violinist Marisol Vega to survive his family's reunion weekend. What begins as a transactional arrangement deepens as Marisol sees through his polished armor, but their growing bond collides with the biggest wedding contract of Isandro's career—one that would save his struggling business and require him to plan the marriage of Marisol's ex-fiancé. As the lakeside festival reaches its final night, Isandro must choose between the career that rebuilt him and the woman who makes honesty feel survivable; he walks away from the contract, publicly and at great cost, and chooses truth over safety. The book ends one year later at a small, imperfect wedding—his own—where he finally believes in the vows he once only sold.
about_author: Hazel Delacroix is a former event coordinator who spent a decade behind the scenes of other people's happily-ever-afters before turning her observations into fiction. She writes romance from a converted boathouse in upstate New York, where she insists every love story deserves both a soundtrack and a second chance.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold Forever
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He orchestrates a flawless society wedding while privately flinching at every vow, revealing the burnout and heartbreak beneath his professionalism. His business is three missed payments from collapse. Emotional beat: competent exterior, hollow interior—the reader learns what weddings cost him.

chapters.title: Reunion Summons
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A letter from his mother announces the Hartwell family reunion, where his successful cousins will measure him against the engagement that imploded three years ago. His sister begs him to bring someone—anyone. Emotional beat: dread and old shame resurfacing.

chapters.title: A Violin in the Rain
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Busking outside Isandro's office during a downpour, she witnesses him quietly pay for a stranger's broken instrument string. Their first conversation is sharp, funny, unexpectedly honest. Emotional beat: two guarded people recognizing each other's armor.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He proposes the fake-date arrangement with a literal contract—he can't help himself—and Marisol counters with terms of her own: no lying about anything except their relationship status. Emotional beat: playful negotiation masking mutual loneliness.

chapters.title: Arrival at Larkspur Lake
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating. They arrive at the family lake house, rehearse their cover story on the dock, and are immediately ambushed by Isandro's relentlessly curious grandmother. Emotional beat: performance beginning, chemistry already leaking through.

chapters.title: The Cousins' Table
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. First family dinner: his cousin parades her perfect marriage, an aunt brings up 'the incident,' and Marisol deflects with a story so warm it startles everyone—including Isandro. Emotional beat: humiliation transmuted into gratitude.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Over stolen slices of pie on the porch, the fake date stops feeling fake; she asks why he really stopped believing in weddings, and he almost answers. A near-kiss interrupted by his mother. Emotional beat: the blurb's pivot—too real by dessert.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Morning run turned confession walk; he tells Marisol about the abandoned engagement and the fiancée who left when his business failed. Marisol admits she recognizes the pattern—she has her own unfinished history. Emotional beat: trust built on shared damage.

chapters.title: Marisol's Silence
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Alone, she reveals to the reader (not Isandro) that her ex-fiancé Theo is remarrying—and that she fled her orchestra life after he took everything, including her confidence. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening; she knows something he doesn't.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Back home, the offer arrives: plan the wedding of Theo Aldana, music producer, the largest contract of Isandro's career—the one that saves his company. Then he sees the groom's photo. It's Marisol's ex. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Isandro hides the contract; Marisol senses his distance. She accepts a festival headline slot that conflicts with his planning schedule, forcing them both into secrets. Emotional beat: the fake couple becoming genuinely dishonest with each other.

chapters.title: Tasting Menu
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. First meeting with Theo, who is charming, controlling, and casually cruel about 'a violinist I used to know.' Isandro swallows his anger and signs. Emotional beat: complicity—the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Festival Lights
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Her festival opening night; Isandro attends, and watching her perform cracks something open in him. Afterwards they're nearly caught kissing by a tabloid photographer hired for Theo's wedding buzz. Emotional beat: desire outrunning caution.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Theo shows Isandro the kiss photo and offers a devil's trade: bury it, keep the contract—but fire Marisol from the festival lineup, which Theo's label controls. Emotional beat: blackmail; duty weaponized against love.

chapters.title: What She Sees
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She discovers the contract and the photo deal independently, confronting Isandro not with rage but with devastating clarity: 'You'd rather protect your business than tell me the truth.' Emotional beat: the midpoint wound—seen completely, and found wanting.

chapters.title: Three Years of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Rock bottom: he drafts the email firing Marisol from the festival, then reads his old engagement letters and realizes he's repeating the exact pattern that broke him—choosing survival over truth. Emotional beat: recognition and resolve.

chapters.title: The Walk-Away
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Climax part one: he terminates the Theo contract, forfeiting his company's lifeline, and tells Marisol everything before she hears it elsewhere. She doesn't forgive him yet—but she stays in the room. Emotional beat: costly honesty, the theme's answer.

chapters.title: Last Night of the Festival
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Marisol plays the closing set; Isandro, now unemployed, works the stage crew for free. In front of the crowd, between songs, she tells the audience the true story of their fake date. Emotional beat: public truth replacing private performance.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Consequences land: Isandro loses the firm but keeps his team as freelancers; Marisol gets her festival slot back and a record offer of her own. They date slowly, deliberately, no contracts this time. Emotional beat: rebuilding without armor.

chapters.title: The Proposal That Isn't One
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At Larkspur Lake one year later, he plans a 'wedding' for his grandmother's anniversary that is secretly about them; Marisol sees through it instantly and proposes first, mid-toast. Emotional beat: joy earned through clarity—she still sees clearly.

chapters.title: Vows
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Their small, imperfect wedding: rain, a wobbly arch, his whole skeptical family weeping. Isandro writes vows that admit he once didn't believe, and means every word now. Emotional beat: full-circle resolution; belief restored.

chapters.title: Songbook
chapters.summary: Brief dual epilogue. A year into marriage, they keep a shared notebook—her setlists, his client apologies-turned-love-letters. Final image: Isandro planning someone else's wedding again, but this time whistling, unafraid. Emotional beat: peace; the song continues.
